title: Early Australian jazz: Graham Bell and the Southern Jazz Group
summary: Melbourne's Graham Bell band and Adelaide's Southern Jazz Group are described as the first Australian jazz bands, modelled on Lu Watters and King Oliver.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Yes. There was, um, just at that time, uh, Graham Bell was starting to, uh, get a few jobs and play around, uh, at a few dances. And, uh, this would be the early forties. Um, he, his brother Roger, Ade Monsborough, and, uh, a clarinet player called Pixie Roberts, were the, the first, uh, first line, I'd say, of, uh, Australian jazz. It was in Melbourne, Australia, that it all, uh, seemed to get going. Um, Graham organized his band after the war, and, uh, they did a trip to Czechoslovakia to a world youth festival. Um, yeah. They went on to England, started the first English Jazz Club, I believe. Um, but by the time they came back to Australia, um, quite a few other bands had, uh, got going. Um, and there was quite, quite a bit of interest in, in jazz for a while. I suppose next, uh, to Graham Bell's band would, uh, come the Southern Jazz Group from, uh, Adelaide, South Australia, run by Dave Delwitz, who played trombone. Um, with a very, um, very fine trumpeter, Bill Munro, and, uh, Bruce Gray, an excellent clarinetist. Um. Um. Um. They were the...
How did they sound, uh, the, uh, Southern Jazz Group and Graham Bell? Are they... would you think that they had any particular model, or...?

Well, the, the Graham Bell band, uh, was styled more on the Lou Waters type than anything else, with the peculiarly Australian sound, uh, I always think. It might be Roger Bell's trumpet, that's the quarter there. Um. Um. The... Southern Jazz Group were, were less, uh, less stilted, I'd say. Um. Had a wonderful, uh, tuba player, Bob Wright. Very, uh, very good player.

I still, when I listen to them, I think, you know, of this King Oliver, and, uh, I think, uh, King Oliver influence, coming down through waters and all that. Yes. When I, what a little I've heard of them, you know. Mm. They're still in that general framework, huh?
